analysis.title: Europe Open - Hitting refresh
key_insights: Asia stocks recovered at the start of the week, with the Nikkei outperforming. US equity futures were slightly higher overnight. USD and UST were modestly weaker, with volumes low because of onshore holidays in Singapore.

NZD was the best performer after the weekend election produced no clear winner. National is expected to form a center-right coalition, with official results due Nov 27. Citi economists put a 55% chance on the center-right retaining power.

Preliminary counts give the National, ACT and NZ First coalition a 2-seat majority (67 seats). About 400,000 uncounted special votes historically favor center-left parties and could cost National 2 seats. A National-led win would preserve the RBNZ's single inflation mandate and a smaller fiscal footprint, supporting NZD and bonds. A Labour coalition would reinstate full employment into monetary policy.

Israel's President Herzog gave Eisenkot up to six weeks to form a coalition above 61 seats. If he fails, Netanyahu gets the opportunity. Citi sees a long coalition process as already priced, so ILS will follow broader risk and tech sentiment.

Oil fell about 2% after Trump said renewed military action against Iran is 'highly unlikely' if negotiations produce a strong agreement covering Iran's nuclear program and reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The US keeps three aircraft carriers in the region. Rubio said Tehran's demands so far are unacceptable.

Conviction is expected to stay low into US CPI tomorrow. Citi economists expect a below-consensus core CPI of 0.19% MoM, followed by PPI on Friday. They say neither print should move market pricing away from an FOMC December hike.

Citi's equity trading strategist says SXXP is just 2% from all-time highs despite last week's AI trouble. The strategist stays cautious and alert to Iran deal squeeze risk, which the desk prefers to play through its CGDOSOHO basket.

Citi's US team is not buying dips yet in this positioning-driven selloff and expects elevated headline risk around the AI infrastructure cycle. It recommends strong vs. weak balance sheet stocks (CGP3PROB) and Health Care AI (CGUSHCAI) as a safer way to own growth.

Citi's TMT spec salesperson is watching Nvidia developments and writes that, while Huang remains CEO, 'its hard to see the AI trade marching on in the short term without him'. Nvidia reports on Nov 17.

Weekly Macro Brief (Jim McCormick) says the US midterms were not a non-event. AI regulation and more fiscal spending are likely, so 10y UST yields below 5% look like a good place to sell. The Democratic sweep lowers the odds of Iran escalation, which should cap energy prices. It sees this boosting EM local bonds and European front-ends.

The Weekly Macro Brief sees UK inflation as expensive given a more hawkish BoE. With the rates/risk implied vol gap closed, it recommends being neutral on vol. It also likes paying front BoE and BoJ meetings.

ECB: Knot and de Cos are the two candidates for ECB president. The FT reports Knot saying he 'won't hesitate' to act in a debt crisis. Lagarde warned inflation will likely stay high in the near term, leaving the door open for a December hike.
GBP: Citi strategists entered Dec/Feb MPC SONIA flatteners after the November MPC. Absent an oil correction, the MPC made clear it could hike in December.

China: CPI missed at 0.7% YoY (consensus 0.8%) and PPI beat at 5.7% YoY (5.3% consensus, 5.0% prior). Citi economists see rising risks of 'bad inflation' and still expect deflationary risks to return in 2027E, which could deepen an oil price correction.

vol_and_positioning: 1-month JPY implied vol repriced about 0.75 vol lower from last week's highs, to 6.65. Selling pressure hit the whole curve from both the market and franchise flow. The euro front-end vol curve is also softer.
G10 implied vols traded heavy at the start of the week as risk assets recovered from the recent rout.
The NZDUSD implied vol risk premium over AUD implied vol is starting to compress. NZDUSD is up 1% after the election.
Interbank FX volumes are 21% below 30-day averages because of Singapore holidays. Citi's platform saw leveraged NZD buying that later tapered off.
Rates volumes are around 0.65x recent averages, with buying interest in the front end and intermediates.
Citi's US team says QQQ puts are the best protection for positioning risks, IWM for credit/rates/policy risk and SPX for a high-correlation drawdown.
The Weekly Macro Brief recommends being neutral on vol with the rates/risk implied vol gap closed.
geopolitical: US-Iran negotiations continue. Trump said renewed military action is 'highly unlikely' if talks produce a strong deal on Iran's nuclear program and reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The US has three aircraft carriers in the region, and Rubio called Tehran's demands unacceptable.
New Zealand election was inconclusive. National is expected to form a center-right coalition, with official results due Nov 27.
Israel: President Herzog gave Eisenkot the mandate to form a government. Netanyahu stays caretaker PM.
US, Russia and Ukraine are meeting in Abu Dhabi. Citi expects a breakthrough to be unlikely without Zelenskyy or Putin attending.
US midterms produced a Democratic sweep, which Citi says lowers the likelihood of Iran conflict escalation.
